sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.6031 Of 2019
Order:

1. In this Criminal Petition, filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., the Petitioner/A1 seeks to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.169 of 2019 of Lalapet Police Station, Guntur Urban, which was registered against him and another for the offences under Sections 270, 273 and 284 IPC and Sections 57(1) and 58 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act').
2.

The allegations against the Petitioner/A1 and other accused, briefly, are that on 02.05.2019 at 05.00 p.m., when the complainant along with his staff including the mediators visited Balaji traders,
Hajari vaari street, near Murthy Fashion Shop, Lalapet, which is being run by the petitioner, found the petitioner/A1 in possession of the banned tobacco products, and on interrogation as the accused voluntarily confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the same, registered F.I.R., remanded him to judicial custody for the offences stated supra.

3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.

He relied upon the order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of UDPR,J 2018 and batch,
dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioner/A1 for the offences under Sections 270, 273 and 284 IPC and Sections 57(1) and 58 of the FSS Act are hereby quashed.
5. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.

___ U. DURGA PRASAD RAO, J 01.10.2019 DSH/MVA Chandra Shekar Gudipati vs State Of Ap on 1 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129892241/
